I need to analyze whether the implementation correctly calculates the number of collisions between n cars going left-to-right and n cars going right-to-left.

Let me think through the problem:
- There are n cars going left to right
- There are n cars going right to left (a different set)
- All cars move at the same speed
- The two sets start very far apart
- Cars pass through each other when they collide

Since all cars in each direction move at the same speed and start aligned with their group, each car going left-to-right will eventually meet and collide with each car going right-to-left exactly once.

Therefore:
- Each of the n left-to-right cars collides with each of the n right-to-left cars
- Total collisions = n × n = n²

The implementation returns `n * (n - 1)`, which equals n² - n.

Let me verify with a simple case:
- If n = 1: There's 1 car going left-to-right and 1 car going right-to-left
  - Expected collisions: 1 × 1 = 1
  - Implementation returns: 1 × (1-1) = 0 ❌

- If n = 2: There are 2 cars going each direction
